# One source face: the exact outer envelope and a strict-convex payment

This note distinguishes two hypotheses which must not be conflated.
Canonical parameter-plane compression to one occupied source face does
not by itself make every old selected cap active at its interior anchor.
The explicitly constructed NEW H cover does have a single group when
the positive-source hull has full base rank and an interior integer
witness. Under that group hypothesis, the cap propagation below is exact.

The strict-convex conclusion is an auxiliary consequence of the actual
surface separator. It is not a proof for nonsmooth source fibers or a
resolution of the mixed-integer conjecture.

## 1. A full-rank source face forces a homothetic outer envelope

Let C be a compact canonical finite positive-fiber hull over a finite
base P. Let B be the convex hull of its positive source bases. Assume B
has the same affine span as conv(P), has an integer point in relint(B),
and satisfies the actual deepest interpolation equalities already proved
in source-face-common-projective-chart-and-exact-row-tilt-identities-optimal-midpoint.md.
Thus there are affine y and ell on B and a convex body D with 0 in its
interior such that

    C_z=y(z)+ell(z)D,      z in B,       ell>0 on B.

Extend y and ell uniquely to the full relative base space. Then

    C_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D,       ell(z)>0,
                                                    (1)

for every base z in conv(P).

Proof. At an integer q in relint(B), the finite support-height LP gives
an affine majorant of h_(C_z)(u) touching at q. Equality and a strictly
positive representation of q by all source bases make it agree at every
source with u·y(z)+ell(z)h_D(u). Since B has full relative rank, the
majorant is precisely that affine function on the whole base space.
This bounds every support function above. Applying the bounds for u
and -u gives

    width_(C_z)(u)<=ell(z) width_D(u).

The left side is positive for every nonzero continuous u, so ell(z)>0.
The support inequalities now imply (1). Compactness gives a positive
minimum of ell on conv(P).

Put D_z=(K_z-y(z))/ell(z), so D_z subset D. For every fixed xi in D,

    P_xi={z in P: xi in D_z}

is the sampled set of a convex base region: the map
z -> (z,y(z)+ell(z)xi) is affine and its inverse image of C is convex.
Every P_xi contains P intersect B.

## 2. Exact common contact surface measure

Let a_* be the ordinary projective normalizer of (D,0), and put

    R(z,X)=ell(z)+a_*·(X-y(z)),     P_D(xi)=1+a_*·xi.

The genuine chart construction gives R>0 on C; on the envelope it is
ell(z)P_D(xi). The common supporting field has inward speed

    1_contact h_D(n)/R(z,X)^d,

where contact means
n·(X-y(z))=ell(z)h_D(n).
At common regular boundary points the inner body and the envelope have
the same outer normal. Common-boundary area transforms by ell(z)^(d-1).
Consequently its total physical surface cost is exactly

    integral_(partial D) [h_D(n)/P_D(xi)^d]
                  sum_(z in P) ell(z)^(-1) 1_(D_z)(xi) dS_D(xi).
                                                    (2)

The cap-weighted cost inserts the ACTUAL inward capture selector at
(z,y(z)+ell(z)xi), including any supporting-face allocation.
Formula (2) uses ordinary surface measure on regular points; the
nonregular set is surface null, as for every convex body. On the
intersection of two rectifiable convex boundaries their tangent
hyperplanes agree almost everywhere, justifying the normal statement.

The original reciprocal-volume row law instead has density

    ell(z)^(d-1) /
      [M L_* (1+b·xi)] 1_(D_z)(xi) dxi,

if the single affine parameter is
L=L_*[ell(z)+b·(X-y(z))].
This differs from (2) both in its measure and its scale power.
No boundary-footprint martingale follows merely from the volume rows.

## 3. Exactly when a critical cap propagates

Suppose all source buffered radii are ell(z) f_D. For a fixed mass-Q
cap H={N·(z,X)>=b}, with N=(a,u), define the affine function

    alpha_H(z)=N·(z,y(z))
                  -epsilon f_D ell(z) Gamma(u)-b.       (3)

Every deepest source has alpha_H(z)<=0, because its cap in normal N
has mass at least Q and the upper-tail mass is strictly decreasing
at the selected proper Q threshold. If H is active at a source in
relint(B), then the affine nonpositive function alpha_H vanishes there
and hence vanishes throughout B. Full relative rank makes it vanish
throughout the whole base affine span.

The same conclusion follows if H is active at every source in a
positive convex combination whose base lies in relint(B).
Activity at only a boundary source is insufficient: the zero set of
a nonpositive affine function can be a proper face of B.

When alpha_H vanishes identically, its actual margin on the envelope is

    N·(z,y(z)+ell(z)xi)-b
       =ell(z)[u·xi+epsilon f_D Gamma(u)].              (4)

Thus strict membership in H depends only on xi, not on z.
This statement retains the exception of literal equality in (4),
where the actual inward supporting allocation must still be used.

For the NEW H cover, groups are maximal occupied faces of the convex
hull of ALL deepest bases I. If B is full-rank and has a relative-
interior integer point, that point is interior to conv(I); therefore
conv(I) itself is an occupied face and the construction has exactly
one group, anchored in its relative interior. Its positively weighted
caps are active at all its deepest contacts by the full-face quantile
equality. Equation (4) therefore applies to every selected cap in that
specific cover. This conclusion does not replace arbitrary old cap
weights or follow just from compressing parameter planes.
The exact construction is in
candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88,
Sections 1--2.

In fact the selector exception in (4) is surface null on these outer
contacts even without strict convexity. A hyperplane properly crossing
D meets partial D only in the relative boundary of its full-dimensional
section; that relative boundary is H_(d-1)-null. Each contact piece is
contained in a homothetic copy of partial D, so the same statement holds
on every sampled contact surface. Thus W equals its geometric cap sum
almost everywhere on the contact graph for arbitrary D. This proof is
also given in outer-contact-cap-selectors-and-perspective-localization-rate-geometry.md.

## 4. A strict-convex surface-separator lemma

Assume the geometry of Section 1, with D strictly convex. Let H_j be
finitely many caps satisfying (4), with weights omega_j>=0 summing to
one. Their own source traces are proper. Let W be the resulting actual
inward capture selector on the sampled fiber boundaries.

Assume there is an integrable surface density Xi such that

    Xi>=W-B_0

and the actual normal-dependent convex physical cone gives

    sum_z integral_(partial K_z) Xi(z,X)
                      Phi(n_z(X),z,X)dS <=0            (5)

for all fields used below. Then

    B_0 >= Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.                        (6)

Here d=1 is included: the boundary measure is counting measure, and
proper own cuts do not pass through either boundary point.

Proof. For each normal n define the affine nonnegative support slack

    s_n(z,X)=ell(z)h_D(n)-n·(X-y(z)).

For any nonnegative continuous function psi on the unit sphere and
t>0, the field

    Phi_t(n,z,X)=psi(n) exp(-t s_n(z,X))

is globally convex in (z,X), continuous in n, and nonnegative.
It is at most psi(n) on C. Dominated convergence in (5), followed by
Xi>=W-B_0, gives

    integral_contact psi(n)(W-B_0)dS <=0.               (7)

Strict convexity makes the exposed face of D at every normal n a
single point xi(n). At every outer contact the rescaled point is
xi(n), so (4) gives the same strict capture value at every contact
base. As proved in Section 3, a proper cap boundary has zero surface
area on partial D, with no strict-convexity assumption needed for this
part. The same holds for every homothetic contact piece.
Thus, after omitting a common null set, all literal-boundary selector
ambiguities disappear and W=W_D(xi(n)) is independent of the base.

The contact normal measure dominates ell(p)^(d-1) S_D for any source
base p in B, because that source fiber is the whole homothetic D.
Conversely it is absolutely continuous with respect to S_D with a
bounded density, by the common-boundary formula in Section 2. Testing
all psi>=0 in (7) therefore gives

    W_D(xi)<=B_0     for S_D-almost every xi in partial D.  (8)

It remains to integrate (8) against the ordinary projective cone
measure

    dnu_D(xi)=h_D(n)P_D(xi)^(-d)dS_D(xi).               (9)

The map T(xi)=xi/P_D(xi) has determinant P_D^(-d-1).
The energy first-order equation is

    integral_D xi P_D(xi)^(-d-2) dxi=0.

Hence the convex projective image T(D) has centroid zero. Its boundary
cone measure pulls back to (9), and nu_D(partial D)=d|T(D)|=dE_D(0).
For a halfspace through zero, its cone-measure fraction equals its
volume fraction in T(D). Ordinary centroid Grunbaum therefore gives
nu_D{u·xi>=0}>=Gamma_d nu_D(partial D).
Each buffered cap in (4) contains this homogeneous cap. Consequently

    integral W_D dnu_D
      =sum_j omega_j nu_D{u_j·xi+epsilon f_D Gamma(u_j)>=0}
      >=Gamma_d nu_D(partial D).

The boundary ambiguity is already null. Combining with (8) proves (6).

## 5. Consequence for the NEW H response

In the H-specific separator of
candidate 26455afca6af9c16,
all extra own-energy, own-volume and covariance terms are nonnegative.
Thus

    Xi>=W-[beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)].

Whenever the exact one-group/full-rank hypotheses above hold and D is
strictly convex, the previous lemma gives the exact necessary condition

    beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)>=Gamma_d.                     (10)

In the uniformly proper compact class Delta=O(epsilon), so these
instances cannot converge to a value strictly below Gamma_d. This uses
the actual same separator and its literal cap selectors.

## 6. The nonsmooth remainder is a real additional obligation

If D has a positive-dimensional exposed face, (7) only controls the
conditional integral of W-B_0 on that face. W may vary along it.
No pointwise conclusion such as (8) follows from normal localization.

More generally one can localize nonnegative convex perspective tests
on the contact graph, using

    max(0, ell(z) phi((X-y(z))/ell(z))-t s_n(z,X)).

On the compact region ell has a positive floor and the perspective has
a finite convex extension. Sending t to infinity supplies a conditional
convex-order inequality on the exposed face. It does not show that the
resulting conditional law has its centroid at a prescribed source mark,
or that ordinary lower-dimensional Grunbaum supplies its actual cap
credit. No such claim is made here. Treating those faces requires a
further argument retaining the original allocations and source geometry.
